review.method: acceptance suite run locally with the retail capability; this harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, the production baseline report over that installation, the production ROF mount of GOSDATA/ASSETS/crimson.rof, rustc and Cargo.lock; validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass. The consumer trace is cs_content::catalog::baseline::retail_baseline + baseline_report_json, the same functions `cs-inspect catalog --cs-path` writes. Each row's identity is the resolved .mpg file's own install_file_key and its span is the file's whole extent with the file's own digest; the names come from two sources, the PLAYAVI actions of the fmv.zrd member of ZBD/zrdr.zbd (production container discovery + decode_zrd) and the M (movie) records of ASSETS/LAYOUT.CSV in GOSDATA/ASSETS/crimson.rof, which this stage added through the production ROF mount and the keyed-list configuration reader, classified by the measured RecordSchema::Layout(RecordKind::Movie) schema and counted as video references only when the file-name field states an .mpg name. The layout rows' edge provenance spans are the records' own lines inside the decoded member, located by the member's stored offset and decoded digest; CollectionStatus::source names both containers, and a source that cannot be read is counted under unreadable_video_source and named in the diagnostic rather than failing the collection. LIMITATION: Five inventoried .mpg files (chap1.mpg through chap5.mpg) no record of either video source reaches, so they are counted under the collection's `unnamed_video_file` gap and have no row. They are not unnamed everywhere: ASSETS/SCRIPTS/CAMPAIGNINTRO.SCRIPT of GOSDATA/ASSETS/crimson.rof constructs the chapter name as "chap" conv$(FC) ".mpg" rather than spelling it, and this stage reads no script bindings, so no row is minted from them. Affected content: chap1.mpg through chap5.mpg. Resolving task: Rally #1352 (F14-D.VIDEO-CHAPTER, the chapter-name binding), which gates any completeness or fidelity claim for the video collection. LIMITATION: No row carries a codec, duration, resolution or playback trigger: no original byte read here states one, and reading the MPEG stream would produce numbers with no unit contract and no consumer. Affected content: every video row. Resolving task: F40 (cutscenes) and the media player consumer. LIMITATION: No row claims a runtime consumer, so every video row is unreachable from the declared roots and stays counted in coverage.unreachable_by_kind. Affected content: the reachability accounting of the video collection. Resolving task: the cutscene/script playback stage. LIMITATION: A name is only identity when one inventoried file matches it; the records give a file name, never a path, so a name that matched several files would be counted ambiguous and make no row. Affected content: any future same-named .mpg the installation adds. Resolving task: none needed while the inventory holds one file per name; the rule itself is the contract.
